content.title: About
content.content: Soybean curd, deep fried, consists of bite‑size pieces of tofu that are quickly fried until a golden, crispy crust forms. The interior remains soft and retains the mild, nutty flavor of soy. It is a common component in Asian cuisines, served as a snack or added to stir‑fries, soups, and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tofu is made by coagulating soy milk and pressing the curds into blocks.
Deep‑fried tofu is known as “age‑dofu” in Japan and “zha doufu” (炸豆腐) in China.
The crispy exterior can hold sauces, making it a versatile vehicle for flavor.
Tofu provides a complete plant protein, making it popular among vegetarians and vegans.
When fried at the right temperature, the crust stays crunchy while the inside stays moist.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Tofu supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle maintenance and overall nutrition.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with animal proteins, tofu contains mostly polyunsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of calcium and iron
items.content: Coagulating agents such as calcium sulfate increase the calcium content; soy also provides iron.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tofu is easy to digest and can be part of a diet that promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: It does not cause rapid spikes in blood sugar, making it suitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals with soy allergy may experience reactions ranging from mild to severe.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytates can bind minerals and reduce their absorption; soaking or fermenting tofu lowers this effect.

items.title: Oxalate levels
items.content: Tofu contains oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Frying oil considerations
items.content: Deep frying adds extra calories and can produce harmful compounds if the oil is overheated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Deep‑fried tofu can be enjoyed as a snack, tossed in salads, added to soups, stir‑fries, rice bowls, or used in wraps and sushi rolls. Drizzle with soy sauce, sprinkle with scallions, sesame seeds, or chili flakes for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fried tofu in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze it; frozen pieces retain texture and flavor for about 2 months. Reheat in an oven or skillet to restore crispness before serving.
